newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU refers energy mergers to German authority.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU refers energy mergers to German authority.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had referred two proposed German energy alliances to the German cartel office, saying they raised competition concerns at a national level.

The move affects plans by electricity company RWE Energie AG to take a 50 percent stake in gas supplier Thyssengas GmbH and by energy producer Bayernwerk AG to acquire RWE's share in holding company Isarwerke GmbH.

The Commission said in a statement that the deals fell under European Union merger rules, but that the German cartel office had asked to handle them "because of the threat of the strengthening of dominant positions in regional gas and electricity markets."
The Commission rarely refers competition cases to national authorities, but it may do so if an allinace threatens to give companies a stranglehold on a particular national market.

"Although initiatives are being taken to liberalise the energy markets on the European and German levels, the electricity and gas markets in Germany are still currently characterised by a system of geographic monopolies," the Commission said.
It noted that RWE was supplied with gas by Thyssengas. "There is a threat that the acquisition of RWE will protect the existing dominant position of Thyssengas against future competition," it said.
It added that Isarwerke was the majority shareholder of regional energy supplier Isar-Amperwerke AG, which received a significant amount of electricity from Bayernwerk.

"There is a threat that the acquisition of the majority shareholding in Isarwerke will strengthen the existing dominant market position of Bayernwerk and ... the supply relationship between Bayernwerk and Isar-Amperwerke will be protected," the statement said.

The cartel office has four months to decide whether to clear the deals. A spokeswoman said the office had started investigating the Bayernwerk/Isarwerke linkup before realising it fell under EU rules, but had not yet reached any conclusions. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
